t: The Signature Air System: Can Plus Electric, One Protocol
title: The Signature Air System: Can Plus Electric, One Protocol
description: The Signature air system pairs a metered-trigger duster can (field and precision work) with a compact electric blower (bench deep cleans) under one protocol card — the card says which tool for which job, so nobody wastes can gas on a job the blower does free. It is the honest answer to cans-vs-electric: both, each where it wins, decided by the protocol not by habit.

demo.program:
print("Can: field + precision (metered trigger). Blower: bench deep cleans.")
print("Protocol card decides per job: nobody wastes can gas where blower is free.")
print("Honest answer to cans-vs-electric: both, each where it wins.")

title: Signature Metered Trigger
description: The Signature can's trigger meters in three stages — puff, burst, blast — instead of the usual all-or-nothing. Puffs clear ports and keyboards without wasting gas; blasts move heatsink dust. Metering stretches a can 30-40 percent further because every job gets exactly the air it needs. The trigger is the efficiency feature cans never had.

demo.program:
print("3-stage trigger: puff (ports/keys) / burst (general) / blast (heatsinks).")
print("Every job gets exactly the air it needs: 30-40% more jobs per can.")
print("The efficiency feature cans never had: metering.")

title: Signature Anti-Tilt Valve
description: The Signature valve draws vapor from a floating pickup that follows the can's orientation — tilt it 45 degrees and it still sprays vapor, not liquid. It does not make upside-down use safe (nothing does), but it ends the accidental liquid spray from normal angled work inside cases. The tilt problem that ruins boards becomes a non-issue.

demo.program:
print("Floating pickup follows orientation: vapor at 45-degree tilts.")
print("Accidental liquid spray from angled case work: eliminated.")
print("(Upside-down still unsafe: physics. But normal angles are now safe.)")

t: Signature Blower: Bench Electric With Filtered Intake
title: Signature Blower: Bench Electric With Filtered Intake

title: Signature Cleaning Protocol Card
description: The protocol card on the station: quarterly no-teardown (blower), annual deep clean outside (blower + can for crevices), new-case blowout (blower), field work (can, metered puffs). t: Signature vs Cans Alone vs Electric Alone
title: Signature vs Cans Alone vs Electric Alone
description: Cans alone: precise but pricey per use and chill-limited. Electric alone: free air but bulky for field and crevices. The Signature pair covers both with a protocol choosing per job — the economics of electric where volume lives, the precision of cans where it matters. It costs more upfront and less every month after.

print("Cans alone: precise, pricey/use, chill-limited.")
print("Electric alone: free air, bulky for field/crevices.")
print("Signature pair + protocol: electric economics + can precision.")
print("More upfront, less every month after.")

title: Signature Safety Card
description: The safety card states the rules plainly: upright-ish (valve tolerates 45°), ventilated areas, never on skin, bitterant means do not inhale, heat storage ban, aerosol disposal. It also states WHY each rule exists — the frostbite physics, the oxygen displacement — because understood rules get followed and memorized rules get skipped.

demo.program:
print("Card states rules + WHY (frostbite physics, O2 displacement, pressure).")
print("Understood rules get followed; memorized rules get skipped.")
print("Safety that teaches beats safety that warns.")

title: Signature Shop Air Economics Planner
description: The Signature planner computes the can-vs-blower break-even from the shop's real usage: cans per month times can price versus blower cost amortized. Most shops break even in 2-4 months — the planner proves it with the shop's numbers, ending the debate. The planner is a demo in this database: enter usage, get the answer.

demo.program:
cans_month, can_price, blower = 4, 7, 70
months = blower / (cans_month * can_price)
print(f"{cans_month} cans/mo x ${can_price} = ${cans_month*can_price}/mo")
print(f"Blower ${blower}: break-even in {months:.1f} months.")
print("Planner proves it with YOUR numbers: debate over.")

title: Signature Can Recycling Discipline

It is a small discipline, but pressurized cans in trash compactors are a real hazard, and the propellant footprint deserves the proper stream.
